newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico coffee stocks dwindle as crop cycle closes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico coffee stocks dwindle as crop cycle closes.

text.p: Mexican coffee stocks are in short supply as the 1996-1997 harvest draws to a close, with most beans already exported and most other remaining bags committed, exporters and traders said.

"Our estimate is that only 100,000 to 150,000 60-kg bags are still uncommitted right now," said one major Mexican exporter. He added he reckoned only around 500,000 bags remain in the country to be exported between May and September, when the 1997-1998 cycle starts.

The exporter, who asked to remain anonymous, said their revised estimates were for Mexico to produce 5.15 million bags this cycle and consume 800,000 bags internally, leaving 4,350,000 exportable bags, including carryover from 1995-1996.
Figures for April exports will be released in two weeks, although exporters believe they have continued a recent strong trend and will come in around 500,000 bags for the month.
From October to the end of March, Mexico had exported 3,235,070 bags compared to the 2,939,623 bags in the same period in the 1995-1996 cycle, according to figures from the Mexican Coffee Council.

"The harvest is over for all practical purposes," said Marco Antonio Machorro Rojas, the president of the Chiapas Coffee Agroindustry Association, a producer and exporter group in the key southern producing state.
Machorro estimated that only about five percent of beans produced this year remained in the country, declining to give a quantitive figure.

Regarding the Chiapas crop, he said harvesting ended around mid-March. "There has never been such a short harvest," he added. High-altitude coffee in Chiapas can still be picked going into June in good years.
Machorro also criticised Ruben Castillo Fragoso, the executive president of the Mexican Coffee Council, for predicting that the country's crop could rise to around eight million bags by 1999-2000.

"That is pure politics, coffee trees do not produce beans for three to four years after planting, so any campaign will not be producing in that timeframe," Machorro said, adding his own estimates were that Mexico was averaging crops of around four million which could go up to five million with good planning.

Scant Mexican beans have pushed up local prices, even reversing negative differentials in recent sessions. "Right now, FOB Laredo is anything like +15, +17, or even +18 over July (contracts)," the major Mexican exporter added.
"It is hard to find any washed coffee right now...there a few bits of naturals and undergrades...a few naturals still in Chiapas, but basically it is over," he added.
((--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom +525 7289530)) E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
